The Spurs won the game 121-94. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) "Keeping San Antonio as the center point," Salier said, "but looking from Austin to Mexico and every point in between." The team's previous eight games at Moody Center have helped advance that mission. This weekend's visit offers a chance to take it to another level. Formula 1 alone typically draws upward of 400,000 fans from around the world to Austin for the United States Grand Prix weekend. The Spurs hope to get in front of a few of them, along with the deep-pocketed corporate sponsors descending on Central Texas for the weekend's festivities. Last season, Salier said, Spurs games in San Antonio attracted fans from 96 countries. The team hopes to add to that international reach by catching a little of Formula 1's global draft. MORE SPURS IN AUSTIN: Spurs arrive in Thursday in Austin for exciting sports weekend "They are a massive global brand," Salier said. "It's a different kind of platform." Of course, moving an NBA game to Austin in October comes with a few speed bumps. From a basketball standpoint, playing the second home game of the season on a neutral court is less than ideal. Off the court, racing fans, Texas football diehards and NBA aficionados are likely to spend much of the weekend jockeying for position on Austin's already jam-packed roads. Hotels are packed, too. The Spurs could not secure rooms at their preferred luxury hotel downtown, forced to relocate to another five-star property a few blocks away. Hey, not all heroes wear capes. Still, the Spurs players were happy to return to a city that has come to feel like a home away from home. "It's always good playing out here," guard Devin Vassell said. "It's definitely different playing out here (for) our second game of the season, but it's going to be a big weekend. … It's always great energy in here." At least one member of the visiting Rockets was equally eager for the Austin engagement as well. Houston star Kevin Durant played his lone season of college basketball at Texas in 2006-07. Friday marked his second visit to Moody Center as an NBA player, the first coming two seasons ago as a member of the Phoenix Suns. "For them to come down here and play a couple games a year is always great for the fanbase," Durant said after Houston's morning workout. "They love the Spurs, man. And to have such a great young team and trying to connect that bridge from San Antonio to Austin has been great to see." MORE SPURS: Spurs vs. Rockets: How to watch the game, who's starting, who's out Friday's contest is the first of four designated home games the Spurs will play outside of San Antonio this season. In January, the Spurs take the show overseas for a Paris matchup against New Orleans in the hometown of All-Star center Victor Wembanyama. They return to Moody Center twice in February for games against Memphis and Denver. Those unconventional home dates fit the Spurs' broader mission of "meeting fans where they are," Salier said. "We've learned it's important to be present," Salier said. The Spurs also know they can't be everywhere all at once, and taking home games away from the Frost Bank Center can ruffle feathers among hometown fans. "We do have a lot of Spurs fans who can't get here (to San Antonio) but can get to Austin, so it's great for them," Salier said. "It's hard to keep everyone fully happy, but we're trying to find a balance." By Saturday morning, the Spurs' traveling home court will be packed up and hauled back to its rightful place inside the Frost Bank Center. The players, meanwhile, will be headed to Dallas for a matchup with the Mavericks, their first true road game of the season. "We play and then they ship us away and the weekend seems to continue to crescendo without us," Johnson said. "But it's a heck of a weekend for Austin. I think the city's ready for it and hopefully they enjoy it." item.title: DAZN officially announce Devin Haney signing
item.description: It’s been talked about quite a lot lately, almost to the point it’s almost common knowledge, but today DAZN officially announced they’ve signed an exclusive multi-deal with welterweight titleholder Devin Haney . The formal announcement comes directly on the heels of a proposed fight with Shakur Stevenson falling by the wayside. “I’m at a point in my career where I want the biggest challenges and the fights the fans want to see,” said Devin Haney. “I’m excited to partner with DAZN. This agreement removes any doubt or uncertainty about my ability to make the major fights in boxing. I’m in position to fight anyone, and I’m focused, motivated and ready for whoever is next.” DAZN executive mentione that they expect the deal to pave the way for them to deliver marquee matchups for Haney and their network heading forward. Haney, 27, hasn’t fought in nearly a year, last beating Brian Norman last November to take the WBO welterweight title. Hopefully this announcement will have him more active than he has been as of late.

item.title: Brewers Get Wild With Game 1 Lineup; Bump Brice Turang To 5th
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang The Milwaukee Brewers released their lineup for Game 1 of the World Series, and Pat Murphy is straying away from some norms. Welcome to the #WorldSeries 📺: FOX 📻: WTMJ #WinOurWay pic.twitter.com/BATskxO6aR — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) October 23, 2026 The biggest shock in the lineup is where Brice Turang is hitting. He led the team in RBIs this year and has hit top three in the lineup for almost the entire season. He hit second in every game of the National League Championship Series. Turang has struggled to hit in the postseason so far in his career, but things started to click in the last series. He went 4-for-11 with a home run, a double and five walks against the Dodgers. He was a huge producer as the No. 2 hitter, but now he will hit fifth. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Meanwhile, Jake Bauers, the NLCS MVP, hits second. Bauers is fine as the No. 2 hitter, and he has been the team's best hitter for most of the year. He is red hot right now, but not quite hot enough to hit ahead of Jackson Chourio. Yelich is hitting third after hitting late in the order amid his struggles. However, he has a .292 batting average and two walks this postseason. He has been benched in favor of Andrew Vaughn against lefties, but the Rays will likely start four right-handers. The rest of the lineup is pretty normal for Murphy, with William Contreras batting cleanup. He has been the best power bat in the lineup, but is capable of coming through with traffic on the bases in multiple ways. Turang is 4-for-16 against Rays starter Nick Martinez in his career. Yelich is 5-for-19, but Murphy sees something that makes him think moving Yelich up is worth it. Perhaps it has more to do with how the veteran will handle the atmosphere early in the game compared to Turang. Yelich could also be lifted for Andrew Vaughn when a southpaw enters the game, so he may just want to be able to stack righties with him and Contreras against a left-handed reliever. Also, if a left-handed pitcher comes in for Bauers, he would then have to deal with Vaughn and Contreras instead of Turang and Contreras. item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Phillies’ Chase Utley content for now, but won’t shut door on managing someday appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Many fans want managers to bring fire into a clubhouse like the old days, exuding the intensity that defined Billy Martin, Earl Weaver, Bobby Cox and Lou Piniella, to name a few. Chase Utley was a throwback during his playing days with both the Philadelphia Phillies and Los Angeles Dodgers. Would he provide a similarly potent dose of nostalgia as an MLB skipper? The baseball-watching world will not get an answer to that question right now. The Phillies reportedly gauged Utley’s interest in potentially occupying their managerial position, but he declined. While the 2008 World Series champion and franchise great did not care to address the speculation, he did share his current stance on serving a coaching role. “I don’t see real upside in acknowledging these different types of rumors,” Utley told former teammate Erik Kratz on the “Foul Territory” podcast. “I can say over the past several years I’ve had a number of inquiries on my interest on getting back on the field. My answer has been honestly the same throughout. I’m enjoying watching my two young boys grow up. As you know, this time goes quickly, and I want to be around for them. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I’m also in the process of starting a business that is interesting, it’s eye-opening. So, I have my hands full currently. At some point down the line, maybe that changes, but currently I’m happy where we’re at.” "I have my hands full right now. Maybe that changes at some point down the line, but currently, I'm happy where I'm at." Chase Utley doesn't see any "real upside" in acknowledging rumors of becoming a big league manager. pic.twitter.com/qh5Qqfa0yw — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 23, 2026 Utley serves as a special assistant to Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, enabling the California native to work a much more flexible schedule than he would be able to as a big-league manager. item.title: Lakers Make Decision on Jake LaRavia After Ankle Injury
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers forward Jake LaRavia will miss Friday’s game against the Los Angeles Clippers due to an ankle injury he sustained in Wednesday’s season opener. LaRavia suffered the injury in the fourth quarter of Wednesday’s win, stepping on his defender’s foot and rolling his ankle before exiting the game. He appeared on the injury report as questionable on Thursday with an ankle sprain before the Lakers ruled him out Friday. Friday’s game will miss the first LaRavia has missed as a Laker due to injury or illness, as he featured in every one of the team’s contests last season.. Through 82 games last season, LaRavia averaged 8.2 points per game with 4.0 rebounds and 1.8 assists, serving an important role off of the bench for the team. In the Lakers’ opener, he logged 10 points with two rebounds and two assists. Oct 16, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers forward Jake LaRavia (12) reacts in the second quarter at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images Who Will Fill in For Jake LaRavia? LaRavia may be missing the second game of the year, but the Lakers made sure to reinforce their forward depth during the offseason, so they won’t miss him too much. Ziaire Williams started the first game of the season and is in line for a second consecutive start after joining the team this winter, and Quentin Grimes and Matisse Thybulle are behind him as reliable depth. Williams played 24 minutes in the opener and logged nine points, snagging three rebounds while dishing out four assists. Who Else Will Miss Friday’s Game Against the Clippers? LaRavia isn’t the only one on the injury report for Friday’s game, as Cameron Carr is also set to miss out on the contest. Carr had a strong preseason after the Lakers selected him in the first round of this past draft, but he’s yet to make his official NBA debut after dealing with an oblique strain. Collin Sexton won’t be missing the game after sitting out in the opener with a soleus strain, though, so the Lakers have some added quality coming off of the bench to supplement their back court in the second game of the season. With some of their new faces stepping into bigger roles, the Lakers will look to secure a win over a surprisingly impressive Clippers team heading into Friday’s game at 7:00 p.m. PT to improve to 2-0 on the season. item.title: Report: OKC Thunder add Micah Peavy to two-way contract
item.description: After just two games into the 2026-27 regular season, the Oklahoma City Thunder will look to shake up their roster. They have reportedly signed Micah Peavy to a two-way contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania. Remains to be seen whose spot he takes, but the most likely candidate is Otega Oweh — who sustained a season-ending torn Achilles tendon in preseason. Peavy is a 2025 NBA draft selection. He was the No. 40 pick out of Georgetown. He spent his rookie season with the New Orleans Pelicans . He averaged 4.3 points and 1.9 rebounds in 61 regular-season games. He was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies in Sept. 2026 and subsequently waived on Oct. 19. Think it was only a matter of time before Oweh was waived, unfortunately. The Thunder need a healthy player for their third two-way, so Peavy was the best available option. He now joins Brooks Barnhizer and Josh Dix in the trio. All three have 50 regular-season games where they can be active. Also expect plenty of G League run with the OKC Blue. If Oweh does end up getting waived, there's still a decent chance he remains in OKC as a Blue player. He'll spend the 2026-27 season rehabbing his torn Achilles tendon. Next summer, he could work his way back to a two-way deal if he shows enough burst. He was the No. 41 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. Former Pelicans second-rounder Micah Peavy has agreed on a two-way NBA deal with the Oklahoma City Thunder, sources tell ESPN. — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 23, 2026 This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Report: OKC Thunder add Micah Peavy to two-way contract

item.title: Christian Parker’s Dallas Defense Still Failing Despite Big Moves
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys made a massive bet to fix their defense this year, but the results are ugly. They hired Christian Parker, a young coordinator who won a Super Bowl with Philadelphia, hoping he could bring order to the chaos. Instead, the unit remains one of the worst in the entire league. According to PhillyVoice , the team allowed the second-most yards and seventh-most points in the NFL just six weeks into the season. Leadership changed, but the breakdowns did not. The front office traded away Micah Parsons and Osa Odighizuwa while bringing in Pro Bowl tackle Quinnen Williams. They also used high draft picks on Caleb Downs and acquired Joey Porter Jr. These moves were supposed to make Dallas a contender. The reality is stark. The defense ranks among the league’s worst despite all that talent and money. Per the official Dallas Cowboys site, writer Nick Eatman noted that giving the unit more time is not a realistic solution when the product is this bad. Third Down Woes Are Real The biggest failure shows up on third down, where the defense simply cannot get off the field. PhillyVoice reported that Dallas holds the third-worst EPA per play on third down, a metric that hurts the team badly. The Packers exposed this weakness on Sunday night at Lambeau Field. Green Bay faced third down eleven times in the first half and converted ten of those attempts. Jordan Love completed all seven of his passes on those crucial downs. Even when the distance was manageable, the Cowboys could not stop the drive. In the first half, the Packers converted third downs with an average of 13 yards. This is not a small margin of error. It is a complete collapse of the defensive plan. Parker is trying to use his mentor’s playbook to turn things around, but nothing is working yet. The numbers do not lie about how bad the situation has become. More Help Arrives Too Late To help Parker navigate the mess, the organization knows something is wrong and has hired a senior defensive advisor. This move comes after the team realized their first season under Parker is turning treacherous. Patrik Walker wrote for the official Cowboys site that the defense has been ravaged by injuries, forcing Parker to play backups at key spots. The offense cannot carry the team forever. The Eagles are next on the schedule, and their interior line will test the Cowboys’ weak spots. If the defense cannot stop the run or get pressure up the middle, Dallas will struggle to win. The hope is that adding Mike Pettine as an advisor will help the progress ratchet up very soon.

item.title: 49ers face Falcons riding sack surge, Raheem Morris happily scheming vs. former team
item.description: San Francisco 49ers defensive linemen Keion White (56) and Mykel Williams (98) are part of a rejuvenated Niners pass rush; they're seen here during a game against the Washington Commanders in Santa Clara on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. (Scot Tucker/AP) When San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Keion White plays against the Falcons on Sunday it will be four days shy of the one-year anniversary of his trade from the Patriots. Does it feel like he was dealt 12 months ago? "It feels like a lifetime ago," White said. It feels safe to say this: The NFL life White is living now is better than the one he left behind. With a team-high 3.5 sacks during a 6-0 start, White is the biggest reason the 49ers defensive line has harassed quarterbacks despite playing the past four games without Nick Bosa . Last year, the 49ers' front four was anemic after their All-Pro pass rusher suffered a torn ACL in Week 3. The defense finished with an NFL-worst 20 sacks. This season, the 49ers already have 15 sacks - tied for the 12th most in the NFL - and are on pace for 43. The 49ers have nine sacks in their last two games and have had consecutive games with at least four sacks for the first time since 2023. "In the beginning of the year, everybody was kind of writing us off, ‘Oh, they're not getting any sacks,'" White said. "But they weren't seeing that we were getting a lot of pressures. And now these pressures are starting to turn into sacks and we're getting a little recognition." A year ago, White, 27, was widely recognized as a disappointment. A 2023 second-round pick, he was inactive, a healthy scratch, in his last game for the Patriots in Week 8 last year. Two days later, New England traded him to the 49ers for a swap of late-round 2026 draft picks. The deal was another bit of upheaval for White, who had played for three head coaches in his two-plus years in New England. He was drafted by Bill Belichick, then in his 24th season with the Patriots. "Bill was there for a million years," White said. "So I said, ‘At least I know who my coach is going to be. (Scot Tucker/AP) When San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Keion White plays against the Falcons on Sunday it will be four days shy of the one-year anniversary of his trade from the Patriots. Does it feel like he was dealt 12 months ago? "It feels like a lifetime ago," White said. It feels safe to say this: The NFL life White is living now is better than the one he left behind. With a team-high 3.5 sacks during a 6-0 start, White is the biggest reason the 49ers defensive line has harassed quarterbacks despite playing the past four games without Nick Bosa . Last year, the 49ers' front four was anemic after their All-Pro pass rusher suffered a torn ACL in Week 3. The defense finished with an NFL-worst 20 sacks. This season, the 49ers already have 15 sacks - tied for the 12th most in the NFL - and are on pace for 43. The 49ers have nine sacks in their last two games and have had consecutive games with at least four sacks for the first time since 2023. "In the beginning of the year, everybody was kind of writing us off, ‘Oh, they're not getting any sacks,'" White said. "But they weren't seeing that we were getting a lot of pressures. And now these pressures are starting to turn into sacks and we're getting a little recognition." A year ago, White, 27, was widely recognized as a disappointment. A 2023 second-round pick, he was inactive, a healthy scratch, in his last game for the Patriots in Week 8 last year. Two days later, New England traded him to the 49ers for a swap of late-round 2026 draft picks. The deal was another bit of upheaval for White, who had played for three head coaches in his two-plus years in New England. He was drafted by Bill Belichick, then in his 24th season with the Patriots. "Bill was there for a million years," White said. "So I said, ‘At least I know who my coach is going to be. I know what the system is going to be. OK, he's going to be an ass, but at least he's a consistent ass.' And then, he was gone." Still, White had a career-best five sacks in 2024 while playing both defensive tackle and defensive end. After the Patriots hired head coach Mike Vrabel in 2025, he became a stand-up outside linebacker. He didn't have a sack or QB hit in five games before he was traded. "That's how the league goes," White said. "You get new guys in and they want something done a different way." His 12 months with the 49ers haven't been without adversity. In February, White was shot in the ankle at a San Francisco nightclub during a private Super Bowl party he was hosting. Four men were arrested in connection with the shooting last week. White required surgery and was sidelined until he made his training camp debut on Aug. 25. On the field, White has welcomed his new team's approach, with the 49ers asking him to reprise the inside/outside role he had in 2024. White has played 183 snaps at defensive end, and 54 at defensive tackle. Last week, he combined with rookie pass rusher Romello Height for a walk-off sack in a 23-17 win against the Commanders. A year after he was sent packing, he's sealing victories. "Finishing a game," White said, "there's nothing like it." Battling Bijan: Linebacker Fred Warner broke his ankle in Week 6 last year. The next week: The 49ers hosted the Falcons and Bijan Robinson. "I was looking forward to that matchup," Warner said. The first meeting between the All-Pro linebacker and the All-Pro running back will take place Sunday. Robinson, 24, a dual-purpose threat, leads the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage. Last season, he had a league-best 2,298 scrimmage yards, the 12th most in NFL history. Where does Robinson rank Warner among linebackers? "He's the best," Robinson said. "No one is better than him at his position." San Francisco 49ers defenders combine to bring down Atlanta Falcons star running back Bijan Robinson during the 49ers' 20-10 win at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara on Sunday, October 19, 2025. (Scott Strazzante/S.F. Chronicle) Even without Warner on the field, Robinson wasn't at his best against the 49ers last season. He was limited to 92 total yards, his fourth-fewest of the season, and averaged 2.9 yards on 14 carries. Asked this week about the most elusive running back he's faced, Warner named Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs. It's possible his answer could change after meeting Robinson on Sunday. "He's obviously one of the best in the league," Warner said. "I've got a lot of respect for him. His ability to affect the run and the pass game is a huge problem." Few know Robinson better than Niners defensive coordinator Raheem Morris (and former Falcons head coach), who on Thursday called Robinson "arguably the best player in the National Football League." Morris has compared Robinson to Christian McCaffrey , because of their unique abilities to impact the run and pass game. "He's one of those guys that can take this league by storm and do really special things," Morris said. "He's going to present a big-time challenge for us this week, and we got to go out there and accept it." Raheem's revenge? The 49ers' first-year defensive coordinator will return to his former place of work Sunday with little desire for vengeance. At least that's what he's saying publicly. Atlanta fired Morris in January after he turned in a pair of 8-9 seasons as head coach. He took a diplomatic approach Thursday when asked about his former team, and was was complimentary of Falcons 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr., who has battled a plethora of injuries over his first two-plus NFL seasons. "Loved the kid," Morris said of Penix, who missed the Falcons' first two games this season while recovering from a torn ACL, but has since helped stabilize Atlanta's offense. "Loved everything about him, the personality, who he was, the thrower. "Unfortunately, he had some injury history. … Now he's ready to go. He's back healthy, and he's probably in everything that you thought and hoped for." San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris speaks to the media ahead of practice, Sept. 8, 2026, in Melbourne, Australia. (Asanka Brendon Ratnayake/Associated Press) Beyond Penix, Morris will have a leg up in game planning for all of his former players: "It's always helpful to know who people are," he said. While he might use his firing as internal motivation on Sunday, Morris has made it clear he doesn't hold any grudges. The 50-year-old appears to be at peace in his current role. He scoffed at a question last week when asked if he has any desire to one day become a head coach again. "We have somewhere in society been screwed up, right?" Morris said as he took a swig of water, a grin on his face. "We have got this illusion in our head that everybody's a head coach. Guys, there are 32 head coaches in the National Football League. item.title: Bills’ Josh Allen gets backhanded compliment in Colin Cowherd’s Caleb Williams praise
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Bills’ Josh Allen gets backhanded compliment in Colin Cowherd’s Caleb Williams praise appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills probably believe they have the best quarterback in the league, and they definitely have the right to feel so. Josh Allen continues to do the impossible every week, and whether he’s making a play with his arm or his legs, he’s still leading the Bills to victories. There is another quarterback that may be trying to climb up the rankings, and it’s Caleb Williams . Since the Chicago Bears’ quarterback returned from injury last week, he’s reminded people that he can do some amazing stuff as well. He showed it against the New England Patriots, who have one of the best defenses in the league. Colin Cowherd was impressed with Williams’ performance, and while giving him praise, he gave Allen a backhanded compliment. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Everybody is afraid to say it, I’m not. I think Caleb [Williams] is the most talented QB in this league… It’s like watching Josh Allen without the interceptions,” Cowherd said. “Josh Allen played New England’s defense and ended with a passer rating in the 80s. Caleb was at 117 last night in a short week. The second-highest passer rating in the Vrabel era,” Cowherd continued. "Everybody is afraid to say it, I'm not. I think Caleb [Williams] is the most talented QB in this league… It’s like watching Josh Allen without the interceptions.” Colin Cowherd with HIGH praise for the Bears QB after their TNF win 👀 (via @TheHerd ) pic.twitter.com/GmdPJhsmiu — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 23, 2026 Williams definitely made it look easy against the Patriots, but Allen is still on another level despite his performance against the same team. Just a week ago, Allen made a crazy shovel pass to Keon Coleman for a touchdown, and almost everybody was ready to crown him league MVP again. If he continues to play at the level he is now, it wouldn’t be a surprise if he won it this season, but it may also depend on how well the Bills are doing. As for Williams, it’s going to be hard for him to get in the MVP convos after missing a few games, but he’s still been playing some good football over the last two weeks. item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.description: Houston Astros owner Jim Crane and pitcher Kai-wei Teng presented bats and jerseys to Taiwanese leaders, including Deputy Director of Athletics Hung Chih-chang. (Taiwanese Ministry of Sports) The Houston Astros have made a decision that could significantly impact the organization's on-field future. No, the Astros did not hire a new front office leader or manager; instead, they signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Taiwan and the country's Ministry of Economic Affairs and sports authority. The agreement focuses on a first-of-its-kind collaboration to boost baseball industry development, player scouting and talent cultivation between the United States and Taiwan. Astros owner Jim Crane and Taiwanese pitcher Kai-wei Teng traveled to Taiwan for a signing ceremony to formalize the agreement. "We want to engage more because we have Kai-wei on our team and get to learn more about Taiwan and to put more resources here to scout and develop players like him to play in MLB," Crane told reporters after the ceremony . Teng is one of more than 20 Taiwanese players who have played in Major League Baseball so far, and Crane suggested that number will likely increase in the future. Taiwanese pitcher Kai-Wei Teng of the Houston Astros throws a warm-up pitch against the Detroit Tigers on June 27, 2026. (Duane Burleson/Getty Images) "Oh, there's a lot of potential. I'm going to go to the game tonight," Crane said. "I've not been (to) a game here before, so I'm excited about that. And I'm sure we'll see some people that are qualified at some point to play in MLB." After the ceremony, Crane and Teng watched Game 3 of the 2026 CPBL Taiwan Series between the Wei Chuan Dragons and the CTBC Brothers at the Taipei Dome. The Dragons won 6-0 to take a 3-0 series lead. The newly formalized relationship is not the first investment by the Astros in Taiwan and Asia. In summer 2025, the Astros hired scouts in Taiwan, Japan and South Korea to increase their presence across Asia. In January, the Astros inked a three-year deal with Japanese pitcher Tatsuya Imai , and Crane restated his hopes of finding great players in Asia. His stated goal is clear: help the 76ers compete for a championship in what he has described as one last NBA journey. Curry understands the business side Curry wanted Golden State to have a chance at landing James and said in July that he would “love to play with him.” He also acknowledged that the Warriors would keep trying to improve their roster if James chose another team. NBA insider Brett Siegel reported in June that Curry planned to meet with James before free agency to discuss potentially teaming up with the Warriors. Golden State remained interested as James considered his options before ultimately choosing Philadelphia. Curry later signed a 2-year, $116 million extension with Golden State after being eligible for roughly $136 million. By accepting less than the maximum, Curry helped give the Warriors additional flexibility moving forward. A rivalry built across four Finals Curry and James faced each other in 4 consecutive NBA Finals from 2015 through 2018. Golden State won 3 of those series, including a 4-0 sweep of Cleveland in 2018. Their rivalry continued well beyond those Finals. On January 27, 2024, the Lakers beat Golden State 145-144 in double overtime. Curry scored 46 points, while James made 2 free throws with 1.2 seconds remaining to give Los Angeles the winning margin. Cameras captured Curry ripping his jersey as he left the court. Green also helped recruit Kevin Durant to Golden State years earlier. It is unclear whether Curry played any part in that early push. The Warriors will chase a turnaround while James chases a title in Philadelphia this season. Curry says he is still happy for his friend. Their next meeting should draw plenty of attention from fans everywhere. Little-known fact: Curry won the 2023 American Century Championship with a final-hole eagle. item.title: Naz Reid brings veteran grit to Hornets for home opener
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets will welcome a home crowd Friday night for their Uptown Opener. The Hornets will be without a few key star players, including Body White and Kon Knueppel, all listed as out. The Hive is still in good hands with their new forward Naz Reid. If the season opener was a preview of what fans should expect, Reid will fit in nicely. Reid told Channel 9’s DaShawn Brown he’s ready for the challenge. “I just never quit,” Reid said, “When things do get tough, I’m not backing down, I’m not shying away, I’m kind of like going into the fire.” Reid comes to Charlotte after spending his entire NBA career in Minnesota. Once undrafted, the New Jersey native eventually earned the NBA’s 6th Man of the Year. Reid says the grind hasn’t stopped. “It just changed my mind completely,” Reid says, “from high school, kind of just like God-given talent, you know, kind of was able to be higher in the ranks doing all the All-Star games and so forth and so on. To where I went to college, it wasn’t the best year, but I felt as though, I mean, I kind of wanted to make that transition to the NBA.” When asked what his gritty mindset means and where it comes from, Reid says it’s a “household thing.” “The little things are the big things to me, diving on the floor, contact, getting the ball at the highest level,” Reid says, “All that is like gritty grit.” When asked about what excites him the most about starting in Charlotte, Reid called it a “different opportunity.” “Also, in my eighth year, I kind of know how it is to be in a play-offs,” Reid said, “I know what it feels like to win a game. I know how to adjust.” PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Everyone Can Watch: Channel 9 & TV64 announced as new home for Charlotte Hornets The Charlotte Hornets home opener is at 7 p.m. against the Atlanta Hawks on Channel 9. You can catch the pregame coverage on TV-64 at 6:30 p.m.

item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Mike Evans Ruled Out For Week 7, Opening The Door For Christian Kirk And A Sleeper
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) warms up before the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The San Francisco 49ers have ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans for Week 7 with an Achilles injury. He has been dealing with a multitude of injuries all season, so he could use this time to try to get fully healthy. Mike Evans (Achilles), per head coach Kyle Shanahan, has been ruled out for Sunday's game in Atlanta. Via @mattbarrows pic.twitter.com/e0nAUEepuk - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 23, 2026 San Francisco has a bye week in Week 8, so he will have two weeks to try to get ready for the Niners' next game. With Deebo Samuel also ruled out, the 49ers will be extremely shorthanded at the position. Fantasy Impact WR Mike Evans, San Francisco 49ers Evans was fully expected to miss this week; now the focus turns to Week 9. You have to be extremely careful with Achilles injuries, so it's not a lock that he is ready to return in Week 9. Nevertheless, we are too far out to speculate about that now. All we can do now is monitor the situation and hope for the best. If he puts all his injuries behind him, this could work out for the best, and he can be a league winner down the stretch. WR Christian Kirk, San Francisco 49ers Kirk is expected to be activated from injured reserve this week. With Evans and Samuel out, Kirk could very well step in as the WR1 in his season debut. He immediately becomes the top option with their other five wide receivers out, when you also consider that De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, and Ricky Pearsall are injured. Kirk is a risky start this week, but should have a decent floor and high upside. WR Brandin Cooks, San Francisco 49ers Cooks, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing will all be competing for targets in this game as well. It's very possible any of them could have a big game, with Cowing being a distant third on that list. Unfortunately, it is nearly impossible to guess which one will have the largest role, and it's possible that none of them are start-worthy. We would leave them all on your bench with Kirk back. If you have to start one of them, we'd roll the dice on Watkins as a sleeper. More Fantasy Sports On SI News Fantasy Football Week 7 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Denzel Boston or Carnell Tate? item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best?
